resources.string: FotoFlash talks to the printer over Bluetooth, and this device doesn\'t have it.
FotoFlash needs the “Nearby devices” permission to talk to your printer and send it photos. It never uses your location.
Turn Bluetooth on to print. It only takes a tap.
Pick your thermal printer from the lists below.
Switch the printer on and pair it in Android\'s Bluetooth settings, then come back here to pick it. Phomemo and other Bluetooth LE printers don\'t pair: find them below under Nearby (BLE).
FotoFlash connects by itself when you print. Print a test page to check paper and intensity.
Waiting for the printer to answer.
The link stays open for a little while, so the next print starts right away. Disconnect to free the printer for another phone.
Keep the phone close to the printer until the paper stops.
Only devices already paired with this phone show up here. Pocket printers are often called MTP-II, PT-210 or BlueTooth Printer; the pairing PIN is usually 0000 or 1234.
Allow Bluetooth access to see your paired devices.
Turn on Bluetooth to see your paired devices.
Switch the printer on and pair it in Android\'s Bluetooth settings. It will show up here.
FotoFlash will stop using this printer. It stays paired with the phone, and you can pick it again at any time.
This phone can\'t open that settings screen.
The Phomemo M02X speaks a different language from the M02 and M02 Pro: FotoFlash can\'t print on it yet.
Phomemo and other Bluetooth LE printers don\'t pair in Android\'s settings: search for them here, with the printer on and close by.
Tap Search to find the Bluetooth LE printers that are switched on nearby.
No Bluetooth LE printer found. Switch it on, keep it close to the phone and try again. If it\'s connected to another phone or app, disconnect it there first.
Searching for nearby printers needs the “Nearby devices” permission. FotoFlash doesn\'t use it to know where you are.
On this Android version, searching for Bluetooth LE printers needs the location permission. FotoFlash never uses or stores your location.
On this Android version a Bluetooth LE search finds nothing unless Location is on. You can turn it off again once the printer is chosen.
Turn on Bluetooth to search for nearby printers.
The search didn\'t start. Try again in a few seconds; if it keeps happening, switch Bluetooth off and on again.
FotoFlash recognises the printer from its name; if it gets it wrong, pick the right one here.
BlueTooth Printer, Netum and most pocket printers
The classic M02 (not Pro, not S)
From its name this looks like a “%1$s”.
This driver usually talks over Bluetooth LE. If nothing prints, pick the printer under Nearby (BLE) instead.
This driver talks over classic Bluetooth. If nothing prints, pair the printer in Bluetooth settings and pick it under Paired.
The recommended halftone for this printer is %1$s.
%1$d dots per line. Most pocket printers use 58 mm rolls.
%1$d dots per line at %2$d dpi: about %3$d mm of print.
The paper width comes with the printer model. Prints keep the same proportions as on 58 mm paper.
576 dots suit almost every M02 Pro. Some units print 624 dots per line: if the frame on the test page stays well inside the paper edges, try 624 and print the test page again.
Blank paper after the photo, so you can tear it off without cutting into it.
Only for printers with an automatic cutter.

More heat gives deeper blacks and richer grays, but prints slower and drains the battery faster. “Printer default” sends no setting at all: choose it if your printer acts strangely with the others. Some printers keep the last intensity until you switch them off and on again.
Higher density gives fuller blacks and richer grays, but prints slower and drains the battery faster. Automatic follows the intensity level: %1$d if you never changed it.
Sends the speed command of the Phomemo label printers, never verified on the M02 family. Leave it off unless prints come out pale or streaky, and check every value on the test page.
Bluetooth LE sends the photo in small pieces. Smaller pieces and longer pauses are slower but safer: if the print stops or comes out streaky, pick a more careful option and print a test page.
20 bytes every 15 ms, unconfirmed: works on every phone
128 bytes every 20 ms, unconfirmed: only if the test page comes out perfect
100 bytes at a time, each one confirmed by the printer: slower but nothing gets lost
In use: %1$d-byte pieces, %2$d ms pause, %3$s. The phone sends smaller pieces if the link can\'t take them.
Custom values, set elsewhere: pick an option to replace them.
Block size, pause and band height

A photo is about ten times bigger than a receipt, and cheap printers have tiny memories. If prints break up, stop halfway or turn into random characters, send smaller blocks more slowly, then print a test page.
The image is sent in horizontal bands. Lower bands are safer for printers with little memory; taller ones print a bit more smoothly.
Top sending speed: no limit (no pause between blocks)
Calibration back to the recommended values
Test page sent to the printer
The roll is in upside down: the coated side must face the print head. Scratch the paper with a fingernail: the side that turns dark is the one to print on.
It prints random characters or black stripes
The printer model is wrong: a Phomemo receiving ESC/POS, or the other way round, prints garbage. Choose the right one in Printer model and print a test page.
Raise the intensity and charge the printer: a low battery makes pale prints. Cheap or old paper also prints lighter.
The photo breaks up or stops halfway
Classic Bluetooth: open Advanced calibration, lower the block size, raise the pause and lower the band height. Bluetooth LE: pick a more careful sending option. Print a test page after each change.
The printer talks to one phone at a time: disconnect it from other phones, apps or computers, switch it off and on again and keep it within a couple of meters.
The printer isn\'t in the list
Classic Bluetooth printers must be paired first in Android\'s Bluetooth settings. Bluetooth LE printers, like the Phomemo, don\'t pair: tap Search under Nearby (BLE) with the printer switched on.
Another print is in progress. Wait for it to finish.
No printer chosen yet. Pick one in Printer & paper.
This device has no Bluetooth, so it can\'t talk to the printer.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and try again.
FotoFlash needs the “Nearby devices” permission to talk to the printer.
%1$s is no longer paired with this phone. Pair it again in Bluetooth settings.
Couldn\'t connect to %1$s. Check that it\'s on, nearby and not connected to another phone.
%1$s didn\'t answer within %2$d seconds. Check that it\'s on, nearby and not connected to another phone.
%1$s connected, but it offers no print channel FotoFlash knows. Check that you picked the right printer and the right driver.
The connection to %1$s dropped while printing. Check the battery and the paper, then try again.
%1$s stopped accepting data. It may be out of paper or have the cover open.
The print couldn\'t be prepared. The printer is fine: try again.
This print was made for %1$d mm paper. In Printer & paper, pick a printer model with that paper width to print it again.
Band %1$d rows | block %2$d B | pause %3$d ms
Band %1$d rows | BLE %2$d B every %3$d ms, %4$s
Width check: both side edges of this frame must be on the paper.
Bands broken or garbled? Lower the block size or raise the pause.
